wikis.title: Fagioli installs the MOSE floating barriers at Malamocco and Chioggia
wikis.summary: Documentary on how Fagioli's purpose-built gantry crane laid the MOSE floating barriers and caissons, with project history, dimensions and cost.
wikis.body:
- Free Documentary – Engineering video, published 2 August 2024. It describes MOSE as "nearing completion"; the narration dates from before completion ("around 2020 we expect the whole project to be finished").
- Venice has sunk about **10–13 cm** over the last century. MOSE began after the **1966** high water and was "officially launched in 2003".
- Heavy-lift company **Fagioli** was engaged by the Consorzio Venezia Nuova in **2012** to lay the floating barriers and concrete housings across the Lido inlet, "the beginning of the final phase". The first mobile walls were installed at Lido in **2013**.
- The Malamocco and Chioggia inlets are deeper (Malamocco **14 m** above the housings), so Fagioli built a new, taller gantry crane to lay those inlets' **58** barriers. Each barrier weighs **400–450 t**; the Malamocco barriers are **29.03 m** long.
- In all there are **78 barriers**, plus two spares per inlet, which stand in while a barrier is out for maintenance.
- The project leader estimated MOSE "will have cost in the area of 5 billion euros" once finished.
- The video description says Fagioli laid **19 barriers "in one session"**, each weighing **40 tonnes**. The narration gives Lido barriers at 210 t and Malamocco/Chioggia barriers at 400+ t.

wikis.title: The gantry crane for Malamocco and Chioggia
wikis.summary: Specifications and transport of the 800-ton gantry crane Fagioli built to lay the deeper inlets' barriers.
wikis.body:
- About **50 m long, 25 m wide and 35–36 m tall**, with 26 m tubular-steel trellis legs. The legs were lengthened by **6 m** over the earlier crane's 9 m, and a mid-leg rotating frame folds them for transport.
- Four **300 t** main strand jacks (L300), as many on the transport beam, and eight **50 t** strand jacks to fold and unfold the legs.
- The crane weighs **800 t**. It was built at Porto Marghera, moved onto a ballasted barge with SPMTs, and placed on the caisson using a centring cone, with GPS- and winch-positioned mooring.
- The fishing beam, hung from four 300 t strand jacks, lowered each barrier **14 m** underwater onto its hinge with millimetric positioning. Each operation took up to 15 workers.

wikis.title: Caissons: the underwater housings
wikis.summary: How the concrete caissons housing the gates were built, floated and sunk into place.
wikis.body:
- Lido caissons (each houses two barriers) were built in a drained basin and floated out. Fagioli's catamaran positioned each **12,000-ton** housing over a **12 m** trench, and four 300 t strand jacks lowered it onto bags that were then emptied for a soft landing.
- Malamocco caissons (three barriers each) were built above sea level, rolled onto the Syncrolift and lowered into the sea.
- The largest housings are **60 m x 40 m x 12 m**, around **22,000 t** of concrete. Access tunnels with lifts lead to a watertight room for each hinge.

wikis.title: Operation and testing
wikis.summary: How the barriers float up, and their testing status in the video.
wikis.body:
- Compressed air pumped into a water-filled barrier pushes the water out, and the barrier rotates up around its hinge and surfaces (the "Archimedes effect").
- Designed for medium-high tides of **1.10 m** above average, and tides as high as the **1.96 m** of 1966 (as stated).
- At the time of filming, "all 20 barriers" at one inlet had been laid and raised several times in experimental mode.
- Anti-reflux valves were planned for St Mark's Square, which floods at tides of **70 cm**.

wikis.title: Fagioli removes MOSE barrier gates for maintenance at the Lido-Treporti inlet
wikis.summary: Fagioli's gantry launching system lifting MOSE barrier gates out of the Lido-Treporti inlet for maintenance, with the gates' size and weight.
wikis.body:
- Published 21 July 2023 by Heavy Lift News; source: Fagioli and MOSE.
- MOSE is described as the project "intended to protect the city of Venice, Italy, and the Venetian Lagoon from flooding".
- For this leg of the project, Fagioli was "the inventor, the designer, the builder and final user" of the **CV.02.EVO.C Gantry Launching System**, used to remove barrier gates for maintenance at the Bocca di Lido Treporti.
- Operation steps:
  1. Position the gantry launching system on the concrete caisson housing the barriers.
  2. Lift the barrier out of the water and place it on a barge.
  3. Carry it by sea across the lagoon, unload it, and move it by SPMT (self-propelled modular transporter) into the maintenance area.
- Each barrier measures **20 m x 20 m x 6 m** and weighs **250 t**.
- The first barrier section was mobilized in **three days**.
- After maintenance, each barrier goes back to its installation area, and the cycle "repeats all over again one by one with the remaining 77 barriers" (78 in all).

wikis.title: Building the MOSE surge barrier: caissons, gates and control
wikis.summary: Documentary on MOSE's construction: Fagioli's catamaran and Syncrolift moving the caissons, installing the gates, the Arsenal control room, costs and controversy.
wikis.body:
- Free Documentary – Engineering video, published 8 October 2023. The description says the "7-billion-euro surge barrier" is "nearing completion" and that "today the system is fully operational". The narration is older and gives a **June 2018** completion date.
- Construction began in **2003**. MOSE has **78 floating steel gates** in four rows across the Lido, Malamocco and Chioggia inlets, raised when tides over **110 cm** are predicted.
- Venice has sunk about **25 cm** relative to average sea level over the last century (sea rise of 12–13 cm plus subsidence). The **1966** flood reached **1.94 m**.
- Cost is quoted as **€7.3 billion** (narration), "7 billion euros" (Legambiente's Luigi Lazzaro), and **€5–5.5 billion** for construction (the consortium), with maintenance estimated at **€30–40 million a year**.
- The first test was in **October 2013**, when gates were raised at one inlet.
- At the time of filming the project was about **87%** built, and the last three rows of floodgates were due to be installed by the end of 2015.

wikis.title: Moving the caissons
wikis.summary: Fagioli's catamaran and the world's largest Syncrolift moving 12,000–22,000-ton concrete caissons.
wikis.body:
- Malamocco caissons were built away from the inlet. The consortium built the world's largest **Syncrolift** (26 beams of 57 m each) to lower caissons of up to **22,000 t** into the water.
- Fagioli built a **catamaran** from two river barges at Cremona, with 20 strand jacks of 45–294 t, to move the Lido-Treporti caissons (dry weight **12,500 t**). The first was moved in **July 2012**.
- Caissons were sunk onto water cushions in a trench and set with millimetric precision. The consortium says it laid 18 caissons, "one every 15 days".

wikis.title: Installing the floodgates
wikis.summary: Rolling out and lowering each 210–250-ton yellow gate with Fagioli's fishing beam.
wikis.body:
- Each gate is a **210-ton** steel box ("almost 250 metric tons" as lifted). Moving one out to sea took three days.
- A four-tower launching structure with two cross-head beams, each with four strand jacks (the "fishing beam"), lowered each gate onto its caisson. The operation was repeated **78 times**.

wikis.title: Control room and operation
wikis.summary: The Arsenal control centre, when gates close, and how the city floods at each tide level.
wikis.body:
- Control is run from the old Arsenal. The decision to close is taken about **three hours** before the event.
- Gates rise in groups of four and are held at about **45°**, on hinges weighing **42 t**.
- St Mark's Square starts to flood at **80 cm**, and the city is heavily impacted at **130 cm** and very hard to get around at **140 cm**.
- Closures could rise from about **5 a year** to 100–200 a year by 2100, which raises concerns about the lagoon's water quality.

wikis.title: MOSE: Venice's mobile flood barrier
wikis.summary: The MOSE system of 78 mobile gates at Venice's three lagoon inlets: design, operation, chronology, cost, delays and controversy.
wikis.body:
- **MOSE** (Modulo Sperimentale Elettromeccanico, "Experimental Electromechanical Module") is a project to protect Venice and the Venetian Lagoon from flooding: rows of mobile gates on the seafloor at the **Lido, Malamocco and Chioggia** inlets, raised to seal the lagoon off from the Adriatic during acqua alta.
- Built for the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport – Venice Water Authority by the **Consorzio Venezia Nuova**, a consortium of national and local construction companies.
- Key dates (infobox): groundbreaking **14 May 2003**; built 2003–2019; **last barrier laid down on 30 January 2019**; inaugurated **3 October 2020**; "Still to be completed as of November 2025".
- **78 gates** in four barrier rows; designed for tides of up to **3 m** and a sea-level rise of **60 cm**.
- Estimated cost **€5.496 billion**, "up €1.3 billion from initial cost projections".
- Missed completion deadlines of 2011, 2018 and 2021; "now to be finished in 2025".

wikis.title: Gates and how they work
wikis.summary: The 78 gates, their rows, dimensions, hinges and raising procedure.
wikis.body:
- 78 gates in four rows: at the Lido inlet, **21** (north, Lido–Treporti) and **20** (south, Lido–San Nicolò), joined by an artificial island that houses the technical buildings; **19** at Malamocco; **18** at Chioggia.
- Gates are steel box structures **20 m wide**, 18.5–29 m long and 3.6–5 m thick. The smallest is 18.5 x 20 x 3.6 m (Lido–Treporti) and the largest 29.5 x 20 x 4.5 m (Malamocco).
- **156 hinges** (two per gate, plus reserves); each hinge weighs 42 tons.
- At rest the gates are full of water. When a high tide is forecast, compressed air empties them, and they rotate up on their hinges above the water.
- Raising takes about **30 minutes** and lowering about **15 minutes**. Inlets stay closed for **4–5 hours**.
- Procedure is to raise the gates for tides over **110 cm**. "As of 2023", they are raised for tides forecast above **1.30 m**.
- 1.6 km of mobile barriers in total. A large-ship lock at Malamocco and three small locks (two at Chioggia, one at Lido–Treporti) keep boats moving while the gates are up.

wikis.title: Chronology and construction
wikis.summary: From the 1966 flood through the prototype, approval, installation of the gates and first tests.
wikis.body:
- The **4 November 1966** flood (194 cm) led to the first Special Law for Venice. A 1975 tender chose no project; the "Progettone" followed in 1981.
- Law no. 798/1984 set up the "Comitatone" and entrusted design and implementation to the Consorzio Venezia Nuova.
- A prototype gate (the original "MOSE") was tested at the Lido inlet from **1988 to 1992**; the conceptual design was completed in 1992.
- Final design in 2002. The Comitatone gave the go-ahead on **3 April 2003**, and work started simultaneously at all three inlets that year.
- Lido north: four gates installed and first operated in **October 2013**; all 21 installed by the end of 2014. Malamocco and Chioggia housing structures positioned by **October 2014**; the Malamocco ship lock became operative in April 2014.
- **30 January 2019**: "the last of the 78 gates was put in place".
- **10 July 2020**: first full test; Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte activated the 78 barriers.
- **3 October 2020**: first use against a real high tide, keeping parts of the city, including Piazza San Marco, from flooding. Activated 49 times within two years, against the 5 times a year the designers had estimated.
- The control centre has been in the Venice Arsenal since 2011. About 4,000 people were employed on construction.

wikis.title: Cost, delays and controversy
wikis.summary: Cost overruns, missed deadlines, the 2014 corruption arrests and environmental and design criticism.
wikis.body:
- Cost estimated at **€5.496 billion**, €1.3 billion over the initial projections. In November 2019 the project was 94% complete.
- In **2014**, 35 people were arrested on corruption charges, including Venice mayor Giorgio Orsoni, and there were allegations that €20 million in public funds went to foreign accounts. In December 2014 ANAC proposed special administration of the Consorzio, and three special CEOs were appointed.
- Opposed by Italia Nostra and WWF. Critics cite the cost compared with Dutch and English barriers, the impact on the lagoon, and whether the system is "gradual, experimental and reversible". The European Commission opened an infraction procedure on 19 December 2005.
- The IPCC's 2019 estimate of 60–110 cm of sea-level rise by 2100 exceeds MOSE's 60 cm design basis. Professor Luigi D'Alpaos called MOSE "obsolete and philosophically wrong".

wikis.title: Baby MOSE at Chioggia
wikis.summary: The smaller two-sluice barrier protecting central Chioggia, completed in 2012.
wikis.body:
- Two movable sluices (Vigo and Santa Maria) at the ends of Chioggia's Vena canal, each 18 m long, 3.3 m wide and 80 cm thick, raised in eight minutes by hydraulic motors.
- Protects against tides of up to **130 cm**. Completed in summer 2012, in time for the October 2012 high water.

## Announcement

- First season: 13 episodes by Millepensee, aired Spring 2023; Crunchyroll streamed with subtitles and dubs.
- Miku began the light novel (Iseleve) on Kakuyomu in March 2017; Kadokawa began releasing it with Rein Kuwashima's illustrations under Fantasia Bunko in December 2018; the 20th volume was published March 19.

wikis.title: I Got a Cheat Skill in Another World and Became Unrivaled in the Real World, Too (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Miku's isekai light novel series, its manga and spin-offs, the 2023 anime, the March 2026 TV special and the second season announced March 28, 2026.
wikis.body:
## Plot
Yuya Tenjo, an overweight, meek middle school student bullied at school and tormented by his family (except his grandfather), is left his grandfather's house and expelled from home by his parents. In the house he finds a portal to another world, Argena, where he obtains power and fights malevolent entities, demons, extraterrestrials and gods.

## Light novels and manga
- Written by Miku; began on Kakuyomu March 25, 2017 (tentative title Level Up wa Jinsei o Kaeta); Fujimi Shobo publishes with Rein Kuwashima's illustrations from December 20, 2018 (Fujimi Fantasia Bunko); 21 volumes as of September 2026; Yen Press licensed it in September 2021.
- Manga by Kazuomi Minatogawa (ASCII Media Works, Dengeki PlayStation Comic Web) from December 13, 2019; 7 volumes.
- Spin-offs by Ryo Kotohira: Girls Side (from December 20, 2022; 5 volumes) and The Story of Kaori Hojo (from February 20, 2025; 2 volumes).

## Anime
- Announced August 2022; TMS Entertainment production, animated by Millepensee; directed by Shingo Tanabe, Shin Itagaki chief director; music Akiyuki Tateyama.
- Aired April 7 to June 30, 2023 on Tokyo MX and other networks (13 episodes); OP "Gyakuten Geki" by Tsukuyomi, ED "Hachimitsu" by Shikao Suga; Crunchyroll streams with English dub; Muse Communication licensed it in Asia-Pacific. The 13th episode's streaming was delayed two days from June 26, 2023 to June 28.
- A TV special was announced October 14, 2023 (Fantasia Bunko Daikanshasai Online 2023), directed by Itagaki; it premiered March 31, 2026.
- "A second season was announced at AnimeJapan on March 28, 2026."

wikis.title: Akatsuki no Yona anime sequel in production
wikis.summary: MyAnimeList news of Dec 18, 2025 that a sequel to the Akatsuki no Yona (Yona of the Dawn) TV anime is in production as the manga ended.
wikis.body:
## Announcement
- Mizuho Kusanagi's manga ended its 16-year run in the second 2026 issue of Hana to Yume on Friday; the issue also announced that a sequel to the television anime is in production. No studio or date given. Source: Oricon News.

## Background
- Manga began in Hana to Yume in August 2009; Hakusensha published the 46th volume on June 20, with the 47th scheduled for February 20, 2026; 15 million copies cumulative in print.
- Studio Pierrot adapted it as a 24-episode TV anime in Fall 2014, streamed by Crunchyroll; three OVAs were released September 2015 to December 2016.
- VIZ Media licensed the manga in English in October 2015; 45th volume went on sale December 2, 46th scheduled July 7, 2026.
- Synopsis: princess Yona of Kouka flees with bodyguard Son Hak after Su-won's coup kills her father, and seeks the four legendary dragon warriors.

wikis.title: Yona of the Dawn (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Mizuho Kusanagi's shojo fantasy manga Akatsuki no Yona (2009-2025), its 2014 Pierrot anime and the sequel anime announced December 19, 2025.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Manga by Mizuho Kusanagi serialized in Hakusensha's Hana to Yume from August 5, 2009 to December 19, 2025; 47 volumes; licensed in North America by Viz Media. Genres: adventure, epic fantasy, romance.
- Set in an East Asian-inspired fantasy world; Princess Yona flees a coup in the fictional kingdom of Kouka and journeys to save it.

## Anime
- 24-episode TV series by Pierrot aired October 7, 2014 to March 24, 2015 (AT-X and others); directed by Kazuhiro Yoneda, written by Shinichi Inotsume, music by Kunihiko Ryo. Funimation licensed it in North America.
- Three OVAs bundled with the 19th, 21st and 22nd limited edition volumes were released September 18, 2015, August 19, 2016 and December 20, 2016.
- "A sequel to the anime series was announced in Hana to Yume on December 19, 2025." A cited Oricon News headline says the sequel was decided ten years after the original.

## Reception
- By April 2026 the manga had over 16 million copies in circulation; it placed first in Rakuten Kobo's second E-book Award, "Long Seller Comic" category, in 2024.
- See also: The Heroic Legend of Arslan, a novel series with a similar premise.

## Announcements (Haikyuu!! 10th Event: Next Step, Sunday)
- Second part of the two-part sequel movie, Haikyuu!! Movie: vs. Chiisana Kyojin, is in production at Production I.G; a super teaser promo and visual were revealed. Susumu Mitsunaka returns to direct and write.
- A special short TV anime, Haikyuu!! Bakemono-tachi no Iku Tokoro, covers the Spring High quarter final between Fukuroudani Academy (led by Koutarou Bokuto) and Mujinazaka High (featuring Wakatsu Kiryuu). It happens at the same time as Karasuno vs Kamomedai, which the movie depicts.

- Source: animate Times; official site haikyu.jp.

wikis.title: The Guy She Was Interested in Wasn't a Guy at All (manga and anime)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Sumiko Arai's yuri manga about Aya Osawa and Mitsuki Koga, its four volumes, awards, sales, and the CloverWorks anime scheduled for January 2027.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Japanese manga by Sumiko Arai (気になってる人が男じゃなかった), popularly known as the "Green Yuri" for its green accent color. Started as a short story on Arai's Twitter, July to September 2021; self-published there weekly from April 10, 2022; serialized on Pixiv Comic from April 29, 2023 and published in print by Kadokawa Shoten from April 2023. Four tankobon volumes as of February 2026. English: Yen Press (licensed April 2024).
- Plot: high school girl Aya Osawa crushes on the masked clerk ("Onii-san") of a record store; the clerk is her classmate Mitsuki Koga, who conceals the double life. Their friendship, formed through rock music, becomes romance. Characters include Joe (Mitsuki's uncle), Megumu Narita, Chizuru, Mao, Kanna, Hime Hasegawa.

## Anime
- Announced February 20, 2025 (with volume 3). Revealed at Anime Expo 2026 as a TV series by CloverWorks, directed by Masashi Ishihama, scripts Rino Yamasaki, character design Kanna Hirayama; "set to premiere in January 2027". Opening theme "Breed" by Nirvana. Crunchyroll will stream. Voices: Akari Kito (Aya), Mariya Ise (Mitsuki) (drama CD, anime).

## Volumes
- Vol 1: April 19, 2023 (English October 22, 2024); vol 2: February 27, 2024 (English February 18, 2025); vol 3: February 20, 2025 (English December 23, 2025); vol 4: February 19, 2026 (English October 27, 2026 listed); vol 5: January 13, 2027 listed.

## Production
- Arai drew wordless short stories to reach international readers; Twitter's four-image limit keeps chapters to four pages. Rock music (Western) is central; Universal Music Japan released an official playlist. Drama CD released April 24, 2024.

## Reception
- Vol 1 sold 150,000 copies within a week; over 200,000 circulation by September 2023, 400,000 by February 2024, 840,000 by December 2024, 1.40 million by November 2025, 2.25 million by August 2026. Dave Grohl endorsed it after "Breed" was licensed.
- Awards: 2023 9th Next Manga Award (Web Manga) won; Da Vinci Book of the Year 2nd place; 2024 Kono Manga ga Sugoi! female readers 2nd; 2025 Japan Expo Daruma Best Romance Manga won, Harvey Awards Best Manga nominated, 2nd American Manga Awards Best New Manga won, Manga Barcelona Best Yuri won, Google Play Best Books Favorite Manga won, Ridibooks Best GL won; 2026 14th Minami Manga Award won.

wikis.title: 2.5 Dimensional Seduction (manga and anime)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Yu Hashimoto's manga 2.5 Dimensional Seduction (Nitengo-jigen no Ririsa), its J.C.Staff anime, a mobile game and the announced second season.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Japanese manga by Yu Hashimoto, serialized on Shueisha's Shonen Jump+ from June 15, 2019 to December 20, 2025; 25 tankobon volumes (October 4, 2019 to February 4, 2026). English: Seven Seas Entertainment (Ghost Ship imprint), licensed June 2021. Abbreviated "Nigoriri".
- Premise: second-year otaku Masamune Okumura, manga club president, is obsessed with fictional character Liliel; first-year cosplayer Lilysa Amano recruits him as photographer; Okumura's childhood friend Mikari Tachibana and others join the club.
- Characters and voices (Japanese / English): Okumura (Junya Enoki / Jack Stansbury), Lilysa (Kaori Maeda / Shanae'a Moore), Mikari (Akari Kito / Jade Kelly), 753 (Aya Yamane), Mayuri Hanyu (M.A.O), Nonoa (Sayumi Suzushiro), Aria Kisaki (Sayumi Watabe), Yoichi Higarashi (Junichi Suwabe).

## Anime
- Announced December 10, 2022. Produced by J.C.Staff, directed by Hideki Okamoto, scripts Takao Yoshioka, character design Tomoyuki Shitaya, music Hiroaki Tsutsumi. Aired July 5 to December 13, 2024 on Tokyo MX and other networks; 24 episodes; licensed by Sentai Filmworks; HIDIVE streams it. First-cour opening "Shutter Chance" by Meychan. English dub May 7, 2025.
- "Following the airing of the final episode of the first season, a second season was announced." No date is given.

wikis.title: A Certain Scientific Railgun (manga and anime franchise)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Railgun manga spin-off of A Certain Magical Index, its three anime seasons, games, reception and the announced fourth season.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Manga by Kazuma Kamachi, illustrated by Motoi Fuyukawa, serialized in ASCII Media Works' Dengeki Daioh from April 2007 (first volume November 10, 2007); spin-off of A Certain Magical Index. 20 volumes as of June 26, 2025; the series "will end on March 27, 2026". Seven Seas Entertainment publishes it in North America from June 2011.
- Premise: in Academy City, Mikoto Misaka, an electromaster and one of seven Level 5 espers, and friends Kuroko Shirai, Kazari Uiharu and Ruiko Saten, before and during the events of Index.
- Spin-off manga A Certain Scientific Railgun: Astral Buddy ran in Dengeki Daioh from April 2017 to July 2020. A light novel of four stories was released June 10, 2022.

## Anime (J.C.Staff, director Tatsuyuki Nagai)
- Season 1: 24 episodes + OVA (released October 29, 2010), aired October 3, 2009 to March 20, 2010.
- Railgun S: 24 episodes + OVA, April 12 to September 27, 2013.
- Railgun T: 25 episodes, January 10 to September 25, 2020; simulcast on Funimation and Crunchyroll; all three seasons and OVA on Hulu in Japan from March 24, 2022.
- "A fourth season was announced during the 'Dengeki Bunko Winter Festival 2025' livestream event on February 16, 2025." No premiere date is given; the infobox lists it as A Certain Scientific Railgun Season 4 (director Nagai, J.C.Staff).
- Themes: fripSide "Only My Railgun", "Level 5 Judgelight", "Sister's Noise", "final phase", "dual existence"; Elisa endings, etc.

## Games and reception
- PSP visual novel released December 8, 2011; iOS puzzle game (July 26, 2013); mobile Spectrum Story (March 27, 2020); pachinko Railgun P (January 24, 2022).
- Four Seven Seas volumes reached The New York Times manga bestsellers list. "Only My Railgun" won Best Theme Song at the 2010 Animation Kobe Awards. In September 2020 the anime had over 300 million views in China on Bilibili.
- A note says it has been suggested that the article be split into a TV-series article (July 2026).

wikis.body:
## Overview
- Manga by Afro, set in and around Yamanashi: Rin Shima, Nadeshiko Kagamihara and friends visit campsites. Serialized in Houbunsha's Manga Time Kirara Forward from July 2015, moved to Comic Fuz in 2019 (February 2019 per text); 18 volumes as of the page's main text (volume 19 listed for October 9, 2026). Yen Press licensed it (first English volume March 2018; vol 17 English February 24, 2026, vol 18 listed November 24, 2026).
- Characters: Nadeshiko Kagamihara (Yumiri Hanamori), Rin Shima (Nao Toyama), Chiaki Ogaki (Sayuri Hara), Aoi Inuyama (Aki Toyosaki), Ena Saito (Rie Takahashi).

## Anime
- Season 1: C-Station, director Yoshiaki Kyogoku, aired January 4 to March 22, 2018 (opening "Shiny Days" by Asaka). Crunchyroll co-produced; English dub released August 2, 2022.
- Room Camp short: January 6 to March 23, 2020. Season 2: January 7 to April 1, 2021. Film premiered in Japan on July 1, 2022.
- Season 3: announced October 2022; Eight Bit, director Shin Tosaka; aired April 4 to June 20, 2024.
- Season 4: "announced to be in production in November 2024"; animated by FuRyu Pictures with Ryuta Ura as new character designer and the rest of season 3's staff returning; "set to premiere in 2027". Infobox lists 37 episodes + 8 OVA to date.

## Live action, games, other
- Live-action drama on TV Tokyo, January 10 to March 27, 2020; second season from April 2, 2021.
- Games: VR Laid-Back Camp: Virtual Camp (Lake Motosu March 4, 2021; Fumoto Campgrounds April 7, 2021); visual novel Have a Nice Day! (November 11, 2021); mobile All-in-One!! (delayed to June 15, 2023); Puzzle Camp (July 25, 2024); Enish camping action game revealed September 2025.
- Reception: first three English volumes on ALA's 2019 Great Graphic Novels for Teens; Eisner nomination 2019. The anime reportedly tripled visitors at several featured campgrounds.

wikis.summary: Wikipedia's overview of MAPPA's 2024 Ranma ½ remake: premise, production, themes, series table with season 3 set for October 4, 2026, and the 12 season 1 episodes.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Second anime adaptation of Rumiko Takahashi's Ranma ½ manga, produced by MAPPA, with Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions handling planning and production. Directed by Konosuke Uda, written (series composition) by Kimiko Ueno, character design Hiromi Taniguchi, music Kaoru Wada, narrated by Kenichi Ogata. Premiered October 6, 2024 on Nippon Television and NNS affiliates; streamed worldwide on Netflix. Voices include Kappei Yamaguchi, Megumi Hayashibara, Noriko Hidaka, Akio Otsuka, Minami Takayama, Kikuko Inoue.
- Announced in Weekly Shonen Sunday in June 2024. "In contrast with the original anime series, the remake censors some Chinese communist symbolism."

## Seasons
- Season 1: 12 episodes, October 6 to December 22, 2024. Opening "Iinazukekkyun" by Ano; ending "Anta Nante" by Riria.
- Season 2: announced immediately after season 1 ended; 12 episodes, October 5 to December 21, 2025. Opening "Wo Ai Ni" by Wednesday Campanella; ending "Panda Girl" by Nishina.
- Season 3: "announced in March 2026, which is set to premiere on October 4 of the same year"; episode count TBA. Opening "Sunao Miman" by Fumino; ending "Kawaikunai" by Yuika.
- Nippon TV listed premieres at 24:55 (effectively 12:55 a.m. JST the next day).

## Plot background
- Ranma Saotome and father Genma fell into the cursed springs of Jusenkyo (Ranma into a drowned girl's spring, Genma a panda); engaged to Akane Tendo; cast includes Ryoga Hibiki, Tatewaki Kuno, Kodachi, Ukyo, Shampoo, Cologne.

## Season 1 episodes (all Sundays, 2024)
- 1 "Here's Ranma" (Oct 6), 2 "I Hate Men!" (Oct 13), 3 "Because There's Someone He Likes" (Oct 20), 4 "The Hunter" (Oct 27), 5 "Who Says You're Cute" (Nov 3), 6 "Kodachi, The Black Rose" (Nov 10), 7 "Hot Competition" (Nov 17), 8 "Darling Charlotte" (Nov 24), 9 "I'll Never Let Go" (Dec 1), 10 "Kiss of Death" (Dec 8), 11 "You I Love" (Dec 15), 12 "Shampoo Cleans Up" (Dec 22). Episodes introduce Kuno, Ryoga (as P-chan), Kodachi, the Golden Pair Mikado and Azuza, and Shampoo.

- 13 "Ranma's Weakness" (Oct 5), 14 "Attack of the Wild Mousse" (Oct 12), 15 "Chestnuts Roasting on an Open Fire" (Oct 19), 16 "Naval Engagement" (Oct 26), 17 "It's Fast or It's Free" (Nov 2), 18 "The Evil Wakes" (Nov 9), 19 "Instant Spring" (Nov 16), 20 ""Okonomiyaki" Means "I Love You"" (Nov 23), 21 "Love Letters in the Sauce" (Nov 30), 22 "Not Your Typical Juliet" (Dec 7), 23 "Abduction of ...Akane?" (Dec 14), 24 "Fowl Play" (Dec 21).
- Storylines introduce Gosunkugi, Mousse, Happosai and Ukyo; the Phoenix Pill held by Cologne.

## Reception
- At the 9th Crunchyroll Anime Awards in 2025, Ranma ½ was nominated in 6 categories including Best Comedy, Best Romance and Best Ending Sequence ("Anta Nante"). Season 2 was nominated in Best Comedy and Best Romance at the 10th edition in 2026.

wikis.body:
- Posted 2025-10-05 by Joanna Cayanan. The 25th and final episode of the TV anime of Kenta Shinohara's Witch Watch manga, which aired Sunday, revealed that the anime will get a second season. The official account's tweet says "第2期制作決定" (second season production decided). No date given.
- The anime premiered in Japan on April 6 on MBS, TBS and 26 affiliated channels; its second part started on June 29. Streaming outside Japan: Crunchyroll, Netflix, ADN, Aniplus, Hulu, Tropics. English dub debuted April 27, with dubs also in French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish and Thai.
- GKIDS screened the first three episodes in North American theaters on March 16-18; Tropics screened them in Asia from March 18; ADN in "selected European countries" in March; Aniplus in South Korea on March 21.
- Cast includes Ryota Suzuki (Morihito Otogi), Rina Kawaguchi (Nico Wakatsuki), Tomori Kusunoki (Nemu Miyao), Koichi Amasaki (Kanshi Kazamatsuri), Kaito Ishikawa (Keigo Magami), Rie Takahashi (Kara Minami), Rie Kugimiya (Syrup), and others. The in-story series Uron Mirage has its own cast and themes.
- Staff: Hiroshi Ikehata directed (assistant director Masao Kawase) at Bibury Animation Studio; scripts Deko Akao; character design Haruko Iizuka.
- Manga: Shinohara launched it in Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump in February 2021; the 23rd volume was published September 4. Viz Media and MANGA Plus publish it in English. Premise: Morihito Otogi, of a line of ogre familiars, is to become familiar to childhood friend, teenage witch Nico, who has a prophecy of doom over her head.

wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on Kenta Shinohara's Witch Watch: synopsis, manga run, Bibury Animation's 2025 anime and the second-season announcement.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Manga by Kenta Shinohara, serialized in Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump since February 8, 2021 (first volume June 4, 2021); 27 tankobon volumes as of August 4, 2026. By October 2025 it "had over 4 million copies in circulation".
- Synopsis: teenage witch Nico Wakatsuki moves in with childhood friend Morihito Otogi, an ogre who is to become her familiar and protect her; she hopes for romance, he does not reciprocate; they deal with supernatural beings and Nico's magic mishaps.

## Anime
- Announced August 2024. Bibury Animation Studios; director Hiroshi Ikehata, assistant director Masao Kawase, series composition Deko Akao, character design Haruko Iizuka, music Yukari Hashimoto.
- Aired April 6 to October 5, 2025 on the Nichi-5 block on JNN affiliates including MBS and TBS, two consecutive cours (25 episodes). First opening "Watch Me!" by Yoasobi; first ending "Maho wa Spice" by Aooo; second opening "Tokihanate!" by Hashimero; second ending "Tsuki to Watashi no Kakurenbo" by Yutori. In-universe series Uron Mirage is featured in episodes 14 and 23.
- GKIDS licensed it in North America; Crunchyroll and Netflix stream worldwide (plus Hulu, ADN, Aniplus); Tropics licensed Southeast Asia. First three episodes screened in theaters as "Witch Watch: Watch Party" from March 13 in Asia and March 16 in North America.
- "Following the airing of the final episode, a second season was announced." No date given.

wikis.title: Sasaki and Peeps: series overview, plot, characters, media and anime
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Sasaki and Peeps light novel series, its manga and its Silver Link anime, including the second season set for October 7, 2026.
wikis.body:
- Sasaki and Peeps (Sasaki to Pii-chan) is a Japanese light novel series by Buncololi, illustrated by Kantoku. It began as a web novel on Kakuyomu and Shosetsuka ni Naro in December 2018 (Dec 4, 2018 start), then Media Factory's MF Bunko J imprint from January 25, 2021 (infobox: 13 volumes; lead text: eight volumes as of January 2024). Yen Press licenses it in English.
- Manga by Pureji Osho in Kadokawa Shoten's Shonen Ace Plus since January 22, 2021 (infobox: 5 volumes; lead text: four tankobon volumes as of July 2024); also licensed by Yen Press.
- Plot: Sasaki, a middle-aged salaryman, adopts a small bird with a star on its chest, which is Piercarlo, the reincarnated Star Sage from a parallel world; he names it Peeps and they form a pact. Sasaki explores both worlds, learns magic, gets involved with psychics fighting "Irregulars" in the modern world, and a war threatens the country in the other world.
- Main characters: Sasaki (Tomokazu Sugita; English Tyson Rinehart); Peeps (Aoi Yuki; English Erin Nicole Lundquist), a small gray Java sparrow. Others include Viscount Mueller (Hiroki Yasumoto), Elsa (Miyu Tomita), Prince Adonis (Jun Fukuyama), Marc (Mitsuo Iwata), French (Daisuke Namikawa), Akutsu (Ryotaro Okiayu), Hoshizaki-san (Rie Takahashi), Shizuka Futari (Naomi Ozora), Magical Pink (Inori Minase), Otonari-san (Akari Kito).
- Anime: announced during the "Natsu no Gakuensai 2022" event for MF Bunko J on July 24, 2022. Produced by Silver Link, directed by Mirai Minato, scripts by Deko Akao, character designs by Saori Nakashiki. Aired January 5 to March 22, 2024 on AT-X and other networks (12 episodes, first a 1-hour special); opening "Fly" by Madkid, ending "Aimai Girl" by Aguri Onishi. Crunchyroll streamed it; Muse Communication for South/Southeast Asia.
- Second season: announced at AnimeJapan 2024 on March 24, 2024; first-season staff and cast reprise, with Yushi Ibe replacing Minato as director; "set to premiere on October 7, 2026"; opening "Unbroken" by Madkid.
- Reception: in the 2022 Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi! the series ranked first in the tankobon and novel categories.

wikis.title: Ranking of Kings: manga, anime, film announcement and reception
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Sosuke Toka's Ranking of Kings web manga, its Wit Studio anime, the 2023 spin-off series, the announced film, and its reception and awards.
wikis.body:
- Ranking of Kings (Osama Ranking) is a web manga by Sosuke Toka, serialized on Echoes' Manga Hack since May 2017 (May 20, 2017) and collected in 22 tankobon volumes by Enterbrain (as of June 12, 2026). Announced hiatus in April 2023; publication resumed in December 2024. Published in English digitally by BookLive on BookWalker; in November 2023 BookLive apologized for "translations plagiarized from pirated copies" in volumes 1 through 7.
- Story: Bojji, a small prince born deaf, and his friend Kage, a survivor of a wiped-out assassin clan who understands him. The "ranking" is a system by which a committee acting for 'Gods' ranks the kings; the top king is entitled to a boon from the 'Divine Treasure Vault'.
- Anime: produced by Wit Studio, aired October 15, 2021 to March 25, 2022 on Fuji TV's Noitamina (23 episodes); director Yosuke Hatta, scripts Taku Kishimoto, character design Atsuko Nozaki, music MAYUKO. Cour 1 opening "Boy" by King Gnu, ending "Oz" by Yama; cour 2 opening "Hadaka no Yusha" by Vaundy, ending "Flare" by milet. Funimation streamed outside Asia; Medialink licensed in Southeast Asia.
- Spin-off: Ranking of Kings: The Treasure Chest of Courage, announced August 2022, aired April 14 to June 16, 2023 on Noitamina (10 episodes); opening "Gold" by People 1, ending "Atemonaku" by Aimer; Crunchyroll streamed.
- Film: "An anime film adaptation was announced on June 22, 2023." No further detail given.
- Reception: over 1.5 million copies in circulation by December 2021; sixth on Tsutaya Comic Awards 2019; fifth on Manga Shimbun Taisho 2019; seventh best manga for male readers in the 2020 Kono Manga ga Sugoi!; nominated for Youth Selections at the 50th Angouleme festival in 2023. Anime got nearly 48 million views on Bilibili with only 4 episodes available. At the 6th Crunchyroll Anime Awards (2022) Bojji won Best Protagonist and Best Boy; the anime was nominated for Anime of the Year.

wikis.title: Akira manga: overview, plot, characters and development
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on Katsuhiro Otomo's Akira manga, covering its publication, premise, plot, characters and how Otomo made it.
wikis.body:
- Akira is a manga by Katsuhiro Otomo, serialized biweekly in Kodansha's Young Magazine from December 20, 1982 to June 25, 1990; 120 chapters in six tankobon volumes. Initially published in the US by Marvel Comics under Epic, one of the first manga translated in full into English; now published by Kodansha USA in North America.
- Setting: Neo-Tokyo, built after an apparent nuclear explosion destroyed Tokyo on December 6, 1982 and began World War III; by 2019 it is set to host the XXXII Olympic Games but is gripped by terrorism and gang violence.
- Plot: biker gang member Tetsuo Shima crashes into Takashi, an Esper child, and awakens psychic powers; Colonel Shikishima's secret government project takes interest; Kaneda joins Kei's resistance to stop Tetsuo, who threatens to awaken "Akira".
- Characters: Akira (No. 28, a child with immense psychic powers who becomes Emperor of the Great Tokyo Empire), Kai and Yamagata (Kaneda's gang), Joker (leader of the Clowns), Nezu (opposition parliament member, corrupt).
- Development: Otomo drew 20 pages a chapter, 40 pages a month at the start, inking directly on submission pages. The name Akira came from hearing someone yell "Akira!" in a studio next door; Tetsuo, Kaneda and the Esper codenames Nos. 25-28 came from Tetsujin 28-go. The logo changed several times over the run.
- The manga spawned the 1988 anime film Akira, produced by Sunrise, and the greater franchise; the film marked Otomo's move into anime.

wikis.title: Akira manga: reception, sales, awards and legacy
wikis.summary: Second part of the Wikipedia article on Akira, covering sales figures, awards, critical reception and influence on later works.
wikis.body:
- The first tankobon volume (September 14, 1984) print run rose from 30,000 to nearly 300,000 copies within two weeks, eventually selling about 500,000. By 1988 about 2 million copies sold in Japan. By 2000, over 7 million worldwide (at least 2 million in Japan, 5 million overseas via 38 issues of Epic Comics), as reported by Critique international.
- Weekly Young Magazine's circulation rose from 1 million in 1986 to 1.5 million in 1990; the 120 issues serializing Akira estimated at 120-180 million copies and grossing ¥22-32 billion (US$170-250 million).
- Awards: 1984 Kodansha Manga Award (Best General Manga); 1990 Eagle Award Favourite Comic; 1993 Harvey Award (Best American Edition of Foreign Material); 2002 Eisner Awards (Best U.S. Edition of Foreign Material, Best Archival Collection); 35th anniversary edition won Best Archival Collection/Project and Best Publication Design at the 2018 Eisners.
- Legacy: considered a landmark of cyberpunk, predating Neuromancer (1984); inspired Ghost in the Shell, Battle Angel Alita, Cowboy Bebop and Serial Experiments Lain, and cited by Tetsuo Hara, Tooru Fujisawa and Masashi Kishimoto.

wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Kasumi Yasuda's Fool Night manga and its Sunrise/Shaft ONA, scheduled to premiere worldwide on Netflix on November 26, 2026.
wikis.body:
- Fool Night (フールナイト) is a manga by Kasumi Yasuda, serialized in Shogakukan's seinen magazine Big Comic Superior since November 2020 (started November 13, 2020). First volume March 30, 2021; thirteen volumes as of June 30, 2026. Licensed in English by Viz Media and in Southeast Asia by Shogakukan Asia.
- Premise: for 100 years thick clouds have blocked sunlight, plants have withered and oxygen is dwindling. Humanity developed "transfloration", turning humans into plants; volunteers receive funds for the two years the transformation lasts. Toshiro Kamiya, poor and paying for his sick mother's medication, asks his friend Yomiko Horai to transform him and gains the ability to understand plants' language, which he uses to find plants on behalf of relatives.
- Cast: Koki Uchiyama (Toshiro Kamiya), Minako Kotobuki (Yomiko Horai), Junya Enoki (Akira Yatsuka), Aya Endo (Saeko Kanaeno), Kiyomitsu Mizuuchi (Jin Hiragishi). Other characters include Ivy, a spiriflor said to be responsible for about twenty murders.
- Anime: announced in June 2026 during Netflix's Anime Studio Focus panel at the 2026 Annecy festival. An ONA produced by Sunrise and Shaft, directed by Atsushi Yukawa, series composition Jin Tanaka, character designs Robert Sato, music Tatsuya Kato. "Set to premiere worldwide on Netflix on November 26, 2026."
- Reception: nominated for the 2022 Next Manga Award (print manga category); ranked twelfth in a Kono Manga ga Sugoi! list (text cut off).

Light novel by Kota Nozomi shipped September 2024. Spinoff manga by Haika Nanasaka launched July 22.
- Seven Seas premise: Ichikawa Kyotaro, at the bottom of the school social ladder, pines after class idol Anna Yamada, who turns out to be odd herself.

wikis.title: The Dangers in My Heart (Wikipedia): manga, anime, film and reception
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Norio Sakurai's manga The Dangers in My Heart and its anime seasons, spinoffs, film and reception, including the third season set for 2027.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Japanese web manga (Boku no Kokoro no Yabai Yatsu) written and illustrated by Norio Sakurai, serialized on Champion Cross; 13 tankobon volumes as of January 2026. Follows Kyotaro Ichikawa, a shy middle school boy who fantasizes about killing popular classmate Anna Yamada but falls in love as he learns more about her.
- Anime by Shin-Ei Animation: first season April-June 2023; short ONA spinoff December 2023; second season January-March 2024; "A third season is set to premiere in 2027."

## Manga
- Began in Weekly Shonen Champion on March 8, 2018; moved to Champion Cross website April 10, 2018; then Manga Cross (July 10, 2018), relaunched as Champion Cross in April 2024. The article states the series ended serialization on September 15, 2026.
- Seven Seas licensed it in December 2020; Tong Li Publishing in Taiwan.
- Spinoff manga The Dangers in My Heart: The Romantic Comedy Won't Start by Haika Nanasaka (focus on Kana Ichikawa) began July 22, 2025; one volume as of January 2026; Seven Seas announced in May 2026 English publication for January 2027.
- Light novel by Kota Nozomi (Media Factory, MF Bunko J) released September 25, 2024; Seven Seas English digital release June 4, 2026, paperback July 21, 2026.

## Anime
- Announced August 2022. Director Hiroaki Akagi, scripts Jukki Hanada, character design Masato Katsumata, music Kensuke Ushio. Season 1 aired April 2 to June 18, 2023 on TV Asahi NUMAnimation block; OP "Shayo" by Yorushika, ED by Kohana Lam. Sentai Filmworks licensed it (Hidive); Anime Limited UK release January 19, 2026 (collector) and March 30, 2026 (standard). 25 episodes listed.
- "Twi-Yaba" shorts released December 10, 2023 as "Bonus Dangers".
- Season 2 aired January 7 to March 31, 2024; OP "Boku wa..." by Atarayo, opening animation directed by Tetsuro Araki.
- Compilation film announced September 29, 2024; premiered in Japanese theaters February 13, 2026 (Toei Company and Avex Pictures), theme song "Madder" by Yorushika.
- "On March 14, 2026, a third season of the anime series was announced at a staff stage greeting event. It is set to premiere in 2027."

## Reception
- Manga: 4th in 2019 and 1st in 2020 Next Manga Awards (web); 3rd in 2020 Kono Manga ga Sugoi!; nominated for Manga Taisho 2020; over 3 million copies in circulation by September 2023.
- Anime: TV Asahi said in June 2023 it had the highest global sales of any NUMAnimation program; widely acclaimed per the article; ranked tenth in ANN"s Top 10 Anime of 2024. Reviewers were mixed on the humor and Kyotaro's early murder monologues.

wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Yoshito Usui's Crayon Shin-chan manga franchise, its manga runs, TV Asahi anime, spinoffs and video game list.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Japanese manga by Yoshito Usui about five-year-old Shinnosuke "Shin-chan" Nohara and family and friends in Kasukabe, Saitama. Serialized in Futabasha's Weekly Manga Action from 1990 to 2000, then Manga Town; original manga ended February 2010 after Usui's death.
- New Crayon Shin-chan by members of Usui's team began in Manga Town in August 2010; since 2023 it runs on its own website.
- Anime on TV Asahi since April 13, 1992, over 1200 episodes, dubbed in 30 languages, aired in 45 countries. As of 2023 both manga have over 148 million copies in circulation.
- Humor: comedy with sexual innuendo (some parents forbid it), mischievous behavior and odd language; most episodes are about family and friends.

## Manga
- Started as a spin-off of Usui's Darakuya Store Monogatari. 50 tankobon volumes published April 11, 1992 to July 10, 2010.
- Usui died September 11, 2009 after a fall at Mount Arafune; Futabasha first planned to end in November 2009, extended to the March 2010 issue (shipped February 5, 2010). New manga announced December 1, 2009.
- English: ComicsOne translated ten volumes (Teen); CMX announced acquisition July 28, 2007, first volume February 27, 2008 (Mature); One Peace Books announced a reprint omnibus April 11, 2012, three omnibus volumes released October 15, 2012.
- Infobox spinoffs: SHIN-MEN, Action Mask, Nohara Hiroshi Hirumeshi no Ryugi (manga 2015-present; anime 2025), Crayon Shin-chan Spin-off, Super Shiro, Freestyle Shin-chan: Kasukabe no Rapper.

## Other media
- Anime by Shin-Ei Animation. Live-action film Ballad: Song of a Nameless Love (2009).
- Long list of video games from 1993 (Game Boy) through Switch titles such as Shiro and the Coal Town (Switch February 22, 2024; PC October 24, 2024) and Me and the Professor on Summer Vacation (Switch July 15, 2021).

wikis.title: Anpanman: franchise, characters, media, reception and legacy
wikis.summary: First part of the Wikipedia article on the Anpanman picture-book franchise: origin, characters, books, manga, anime, films, specials, games, music, sales and legacy.
wikis.body:
## Overview
- Japanese children's superhero picture book series and franchise by Takashi Yanase, running from 1973 until his death in 2013. Anpanman has an anpan (red bean paste pastry) for a head and protects the world from the germ Baikinman. Adapted as anime Soreike! Anpanman, "one of the most popular anime series among young children in Japan".
- Overtook Hello Kitty as Japan's top-grossing character in 2002 and remained top as of 2019. Sold over 80 million books as of February 2019; franchise generated ¥4.5 trillion in total retail sales by 2013; related product retail at least ¥150 billion annually for nearly 30 years.
- Origin: during the Second World War Yanase faced starvation and dreamed of eating an anpan.
- Guinness World Record (2009) for most characters in an animated franchise: 1,768 characters in the first 980 episodes and first 20 films.

## Characters
- Anpanman: head made by Uncle Jam, weak to water and dirt, gets a fresh head baked by Uncle Jam, gives part of his head to the starving; attacks An-punch and An-kick; born when a shooting star ("the stars of life") landed in Uncle Jam's oven.
- Allies: Uncle Jam (baker; voiced by Hiroshi Masuoka 1988-2019, Koichi Yamadera 2019-present), Batako-san, dog Cheese, Currypanman, Shokupanman, Melonpanna, Rollpanna, Creampanda. Villain Baikinman, leader of the Viruses, born at the same time as Anpanman, weak to soap; battle cry "Ha-hi-hu-he-ho!".

## Media
- Picture books: debuted October 1973; Froebel-kan has published over 150.
- Manga: three series by Yanase: Nekketsu Marchen Kaiketsu Anpanman (Jan 1975-May 1976, adult-aimed), Anpanman (Sept 1976-July 1982), Tobe! Anpanman (Jan 1, 1990-May 29, 1994, Yomiuri Shinbun).
- Anime: one-episode NHK adaptation March 13, 1979; Soreike! Anpanman by TMS Entertainment on NTV since October 3, 1988, over 1300 episodes; voice recording paused April 2020 due to COVID-19; English dub for Turner International aired on Pogo in India.
- 36 full-length films released yearly since 1989 except 2020; shorts from 1990; 32 Christmas specials since December 1988; 42 video games (mostly Japan-only).
- Opening "Anpanman's March".

## Reception and legacy
- Bandai research (2011): most popular fictional character among ages 0-12 in Japan for 10 consecutive years. Books sold 50 million by 2006, 68 million by 2013.
- Box office table: e.g. 2018 film Kagayake! Kurun to Inochi no Hoshi gross ¥649,000,000.
- Five museums dedicated to Anpanman; JR Shikoku train livery; first overseas shop opened in Taipei September 10, 2015; inspired One-Punch Man; BTS song "Anpanman".

## Series
- Light novel by Nekoko, illustrated by Jaian: serialized on Shosetsuka ni Naro from April 25, 2021; Kodansha Ranobe Books from June 2, 2022; five volumes as of July 2026 (vol. 4 December 26, 2025; vol. 5 July 2, 2026).

- Anime announced September 5, 2024; produced by GoHands, director Katsumasa Yokomine, chief directors Shingo Suzuki and Tetsuichi Yamagishi, character design Takayuki Uchida, music Ludvig Forssell. Premiered July 3, 2026 on Super Animeism Turbo on all JNN affiliates (MBS, TBS); "two consecutive cours for a total of 26 episodes". Opening "Awake" by Spyair; ending "Lv. 1 Shokugyo: Ningen" by Reona. Crunchyroll streams; Muse Communication licensed South/Southeast Asia.

## Plot
- Elymas Edvan, fifteen, from a family of Master Swordsmen, manifests the defective Heavy Knight class at the Ritual of Divine Blessing, loses heir status and is exiled. He realizes the world matches a game from a previous life, in which Heavy Knight is the strongest class if used correctly.
- Cast: Elymas, Ruche Luvis (Shion Wakayama / Kiane Chula King), Malice Edvan (Natsuko Abe / Katie Caruso).

wikis.title: Kagurabachi: premise, plot and characters
wikis.summary: Opening of the Wikipedia article on Takeru Hokazono's manga Kagurabachi: premise, plot setting and its cast of factions.
wikis.body:
- Japanese manga written and illustrated by Takeru Hokazono, serialized in Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump since September 2023, in 12 tankobon volumes "as of September 2026". By April 2026 it had over 4 million copies in circulation; it won the 10th Next Manga Award (print) in 2024. A Cypic anime is "set to premiere in April 2027".
- Premise: Chihiro Rokuhira wields "Enten", the seventh of the Enchanted Blades forged by his father, swordsmith Kunishige Rokuhira. The Hishaku, a group of ten elite criminal sorcerers with flame tattoos, murdered Kunishige three years ago and stole the six other blades; Chihiro seeks revenge and to reclaim them. Setting: modern Japan, 18 years after the Seitei War.
- Chihiro's group: Chihiro Rokuhira (18; voiced by Taihi Kimura in the anime), Togo Shiba (Katsuyuki Konishi), Hakuri Sazanami, Iori Samura, Hinao (Miku Ito), Char Kyonagi (Miyari Nemoto).
- Kamunabi: government-backed sorcerer agency formed in the Seitei War; heads Kasen, Ichiki, Yatsuru, Soshiro Azami, Izaru, Kudo; fighters Hiyuki Kagari, Tafuku Mihara, Kiri Shirakai, Natsuki Misaka; the Anti-Cloud Gouger Special Forces; the Masumi ninja clan (Ro, Moku, Sumi).
- Enchanted Blade Bearers: Yoji Uruha (Kumeyuri), Seiichi Samura (Tobimune), Ibuki Misaka (Cloud Gouger), Subaru Urita. Soga clan: Chiaki Soga (Chihiro's mother) and her brother Akemura, the Sword Master holding Magatsumi.
- Antagonists: Hishaku leader Yura (Chihiro's arch nemesis), Hokuto and others; also the Sazanami clan and other factions.

wikis.title: Kagurabachi: manga volumes, anime and reception
wikis.summary: Second half of the Wikipedia article: volume summaries, the 2027 anime, sales, popularity and awards.
wikis.body:
- Volume 12 released September 4, 2026 (ISBN 978-4-08-885177-8). Late chapters: Chihiro is gravely wounded by his uncle Akemura Soga and Enten is broken; Seiichi Samura sacrifices himself in a duel with Akemura and sends Tobimune to Iori; Chihiro goes home to begin reforging Enten. Chapters not yet in tankobon include the "Irishima Talks" and "Smelting" arcs (a prequel-style story of Kunishige).
- Anime: in December 2024 Toyo Keizai Online reported an anime by Cypic (then CygamesPictures) via CyberAgent and Shochiku; "announced in April 2026 to be an anime television series", directed by Tetsuya Takeuchi, character designs by Keigo Sasaki, "set to premiere in April 2027". From July 2026 the first 20 minutes of episode 1 are screened at events (Anime Expo Los Angeles, Anime NYC, Japan Expo Paris, AnimagiC Mannheim), concluding in Japan in Q2 2027 with the full first episode. Crunchyroll will stream worldwide except Japan, mainland China, North Korea and South Korea; Muse Communication licenses South and Southeast Asia.
- Popularity: surpassed Spy x Family, Dragon Ball Super and Boruto on MANGA Plus's ranking; first chapter the world's most viewed in its first week; over 99 million page views by April 2024. Ranked 7th in AnimeJapan's 2024 "Most Wanted Anime Adaptation" poll, 6th on Kono Manga ga Sugoi! 2025 (male readers). Recommended by Kohei Horikoshi and Masashi Kishimoto.
- Sales: over 350,000 copies by July 2024; 600,000 by August 2024; 1 million by October 2024; 1.3 million by December 2024; 2.2 million by May 2025; over 3 million by October 2025; over 4 million by April 2026. Ranked on Circana BookScan and NYT manga lists since late 2024.
- Accolades: 10th Next Manga Award print category (2024); nominated for 70th Shogakukan Manga Award (2024), 49th Kodansha Manga Award shonen and an Eisner (2025); Japan Expo Daruma for Best Action Manga (2026).

wikis.title: Toyo Keizai report: Kagurabachi anime at Cygames Pictures
wikis.summary: Anime News Network report (2024-12-02) that Toyo Keizai says Kagurabachi will be adapted as an anime at Cygames Pictures, co-produced by CyberAgent and Shochiku.
wikis.body:
- Posted 2024-12-02 by Joanna Cayanan. Toyo Keizai Online (site tied to Weekly Toyo Keizai) reported that Takeru Hokazono's Kagurabachi manga will get an anime at Cygames Pictures through a joint production by CyberAgent and Shochiku. The headline says "reportedly".
- Toyo Keizai contacted both companies: CyberAgent said "there is nothing we can say"; Shochiku said it will "refrain from responding to inquiries regarding individual works."
- Manga: debuted in Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump in September 2023; fifth compiled volume due the Wednesday after the report; over 1.3 million copies in circulation. Viz Media released volume 1 in print on November 5 and volume 2 was due February 4. Digital English releases via Viz Media's Shonen Jump and Shueisha's MANGA Plus. It topped the print category of the Next Manga Awards 2024 in August.
- MANGA Plus synopsis: young Chihiro trains under his famous swordsmith father until tragedy strikes; "Chihiro and his blade now live only for revenge."
- Background on CyberAgent: founded Cygames in 2011 (Rage of Bahamut, Granblue Fantasy); Cygames anime division March 2015, Cygames Pictures April 2016; CA-Cygames Anime Fund June 2017 (invested in Hinomaru Sumo, Zombie Land Saga, As Miss Beelzebub Likes); Kadokawa capital alliance with CyberAgent and Sony February 2021; CyberAgent bought Nelke Planning June 2023 and Nitroplus on July 1.
- Source: Toyo Keizai (Soichiro Morita) via Yahoo! Japan, Yaraon!

wikis.title: Boruto: Naruto Next Generations (TV series) on Wikipedia
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on the Pierrot anime Boruto: Naruto Next Generations (293 episodes, 2017-2023), its production, release, music and reception, noting a second part in development.
wikis.body:
- Japanese anime TV series based on the manga Boruto by Ukyo Kodachi and Mikio Ikemoto, supervised by Masashi Kishimoto; a spin-off and sequel to Naruto and Naruto: Shippuden. Produced by Pierrot for TV Tokyo; 24 minutes per episode; aired 5 April 2017 to 26 March 2023, 293 episodes. "A second part was announced to be in development."
- The anime begins as a prequel set before Boruto and friends become ninjas, unlike the manga, which began as a retelling of Boruto: Naruto the Movie (2015).
- Plot: Naruto is Seventh Hokage; his son Boruto joins the Ninja Academy and forms a team with Sarada Uchiha and Mitsuki under Konohamaru Sarutobi; the Otsutsuki (Momoshiki, Kinshiki) threaten Naruto; Boruto gets a mark called "Karma"; the group Kara, Kawaki, Jigen and Isshiki Otsutsuki drive later arcs.
- Production: directors Hiroyuki Yamashita (to ep. 66), Toshiro Fujii (67-104), Masayuki Koda (105-281, 287-293); Noriyuki Abe chief director to 104 and series director 282-286; Ukyo Kodachi supervised the story until episode 216; Makoto Uezu then Masaya Honda on series composition.
- Release: announced at Jump Festa stage event on 17 December 2016; premiered on TV Tokyo 5 April 2017; episode 155 onward delayed to 6 July 2020 by COVID-19 (announced 21 April 2020); first part ended with episode 293 on 26 March 2023. Viz Media licensed it in North America; English dub on Adult Swim's Toonami from 29 September 2018; ABC Me in Australia from 21 September 2019; Yey! in the Philippines 16 December 2019 to 21 February 2020 (52 episodes).
- Music: Yasuharu Takanashi and Yaiba; soundtracks 28 June 2017 and 7 November 2018; 35 theme songs (12 openings, 23 endings), e.g. opening 1 "Baton Road" by KANA-BOON (eps 1-26), opening 12 "Shukuen" by Asian Kung-Fu Generation (eps 282-293).
- Reception: Charapedia readers voted it ninth best anime of Spring 2017; IGN's Sam Stewart praised the focus on the new generation.

wikis.summary: Overview of Kocha Agasawa's web manga The Ramparts of Ice, its Shueisha/Line Manga publication, the Studio Kai anime (April 2026, second season October 2026) and the main characters.
wikis.body:
- Japanese web manga (氷の城壁, Kori no Joheki) by Kocha Agasawa; genre romantic comedy. First a self-published webtoon on Line Manga Indies for about two years, then officially serialized on Line Manga (digital) from January 10, 2020 to April 28, 2022 (117 chapters per the author; Line Manga counts 130) after the Margaret editorial department got involved.
- Shueisha (Jump Comics imprint) printed 14 tankobon volumes from July 4, 2023 to February 4, 2025. English: NTT Solmare's MangaPlaza.
- Premise: introverted high schooler Koyuki Hikawa, nicknamed "The Ice Queen", keeps her distance from others until Minato Amamiya, Miki Azumi and Yota Hino draw her out.
- Anime: announced January 2025; Studio Kai; director Mankyu; series composition Yasuhiro Nakanishi; character design Miki Ogino; music Kanade Sakuma and Natsumi Tabuchi. Aired April 2 to July 2, 2026 on TBS and affiliates (JNN); Netflix streams globally; 14 episodes. Opening "Tomei" by Novelbright, ending "Sakasama" by Polkadot Stingray.
- Second season announced after the first-season finale, "set to premiere on October 1 of the same year" (2026), with opening "Escort" by The Beat Garden and ending "Hanakage" by Superfly.
- Main cast (Japanese / English): Koyuki Hikawa (Anna Nagase / Erika Harlacher), Miki Azumi (Fuka Izumi / Brianna Knickerbocker), Minato Amamiya (Shoya Chiba / Kyle McCarley), Yota Hino (Satoshi Inomata / Jason Griffith).

wikis.title: Evangelion franchise announces a new series at its 30th anniversary festival
wikis.summary: Anime News Network report that the Evangelion :30+ festival ended on 2026-02-23 with an announcement of a brand-new series from Yoko Taro, Kazuya Tsurumaki and Toko Yatabe at Khara and CloverWorks.
wikis.body:
- Posted 2026-02-23 by Egan Loo on Anime News Network.
- The "Evangelion :30+; 30th Anniversary of Evangelion" festival ended on Monday with a surprise video and a live cello and choral performance announcing a brand-new series. The project was teased as the franchise's "Next Genesis".
- Staff named: Yoko Taro (series script supervisor and scriptwriter; NieR:Automata), directors Kazuya Tsurumaki (Rebuild of Evangelion, Mobile Suit Gundam GQuuuuuuX) and Toko Yatabe (assistant director of Evangelion: 3.0+1.0 Thrice Upon A Time; Chainsaw Man storyboarder/episode director), composer Keiichi Okabe (NieR), and Studio Khara and CloverWorks as production studios.
- The festival took place at Yokohama Arena between February 21 and 23. It exclusively premiered "Evangelion Broadcast 30th Anniversary Special Screening", a new 13-minute anime short starring Asuka.
- Yoko Takahashi, singer of the Neon Genesis Evangelion TV opening theme, performed an "Eva Fes Ver." of this spring's "Back to Neon Genesis" concerts. The festival closed with a preview of the stage production Kabuki Symphony No. 9 Evangelion.
- The page notes a follow-up article: "New Evangelion Series Streams Teaser Video" (2026-02-23 22:05).
- No premiere date, format or episode count is given in the article.

wikis.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion franchise
wikis.summary: Wikipedia overview of the Evangelion media franchise, including the new series announced in February 2026.
wikis.body:
- Franchise created by Hideaki Anno (Gainax 1994-2006, Khara 2006-present): 1995-96 TV anime, 1997 films, Rebuild of Evangelion (2007-2021), manga, light novels, music, games, pachinko and crossovers.
- New anime series announced after the "Evangelion :30+; 30th Anniversary of Evangelion" festival in February 2026: CloverWorks and Khara, directors Kazuya Tsurumaki and Toko Yatabe, scripts Yoko Taro, music Keiichi Okabe. No release date is stated.
- The 30th Anniversary Special Screening short (Asuka-focused, written by Anno, directed by Naoyuki Asano) was shown at Yokohama Arena in February 2026 and released on YouTube on March 7, 2026 after an accidental leak by Khara.
- 2026 crossovers cited in references: Final Fantasy XIV raid series "Ghosts of Desire" and a Sonic game.

wikis.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion franchise: series, films, Rebuild, the new series and other media
wikis.summary: Franchise overview covering the 1995-96 anime, the 1997 films, Rebuild of Evangelion, the series announced in February 2026, the 30th Anniversary short, manga, music, games and crossovers.
wikis.body:
- Created by Hideaki Anno; owned by Gainax (1994-2006), then Khara (2006-present). Setting: after the Second Impact (Antarctica, year 2000); fifteen years later Angels attack and the UN-controlled paramilitary NERV fights them with Evangelions piloted by teenagers (Shinji Ikari, Rei Ayanami, Asuka Langley Soryu).
- Manga debuted in Shonen Ace in December 1994. TV anime (Tatsunoko animation, Gainax production, directed by Anno) aired on TV Tokyo October 1995 to March 1996; Excellence Award at the Japan Media Arts Festival 1997.
- Films: Death & Rebirth (March 1997) and The End of Evangelion (July 19, 1997), an alternate ending that grossed 2.47 billion yen and won Most Popular Film at the Awards of the Japanese Academy and the 1997 Animage Anime Grand Prix.
- Petit Eva: Evangelion@School: chibi-style ONA parody, 24 broadcasts from March 20, 2007 to March 11, 2009.
- Rebuild of Evangelion (Studio Khara; Anno writer, Kazuya Tsurumaki and Masayuki directing): 1.0 released September 1, 2007; 2.0 June 27, 2009; 3.0 November 17, 2012; 3.0+1.0 Thrice Upon a Time March 8, 2021; home media March 8, 2023 added two OVAs.
- Untitled anime series: announced following the "Evangelion :30+; 30th Anniversary of Evangelion" festival in February 2026; to be produced by CloverWorks and Khara, directed by Kazuya Tsurumaki and Toko Yatabe, scripts by Yoko Taro, music by Keiichi Okabe.
- Evangelion Broadcast 30th Anniversary Special Screening: short written by Anno, directed by Naoyuki Asano, shown only at Yokohama Arena in February 2026; it features both Asukas in a manzai performance. Khara took down cam recordings on X, then accidentally leaked the film via takedown mails, and released it on YouTube on March 7, 2026.
- Other media: Sadamoto's manga (February 1995 to November 2014), light novel ANIMA (2008-2013), soundtracks by Shiro Sagisu, a proposed live-action film announced at Cannes on May 21, 2003 (never released per the text's "development hell"), video games, pachinko (over two million machines sold by 2015, 700 billion yen revenue), Fuji-Q Highland attraction (opened July 22, 2010), Universal Studios Japan "Godzilla vs. Evangelion: The Real 4-D" (May 31 to August 25, 2019), Transformers and Shinkalion crossovers.

wikis.title: Blue Lock manga gets a third anime season and a live-action film
wikis.summary: Anime News Network report of 2025-09-28 that Blue Lock will get a third anime season adapting the New Hero Wars story and a live-action film slated for summer 2026.
wikis.body:
- Posted 2025-09-28 by Joanna Cayanan on Anime News Network. Subhead: "Live-action film slated for summer 2026".
- The "Blue Lock Egoist Fest 2025" event on Sunday revealed that the anime based on Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Yusuke Nomura's BLUELOCK soccer manga will get a third season adapting the "Shin Eiyu Taisen" (New Hero Wars) story.
- The event also revealed a live-action film adaptation of the manga, slated for release in "summer 2026" (2026年 夏). CREDEUS (which made the live-action Golden Kamuy film) is producing and Toho is distributing.

- The article lists new season-2 cast, e.g. Eiji Mikami as Yo Hiori, Kakeru Hatano as Nijiro Nanase, Yuichi Nakamura as Ryusei Shidou.
- Official posts announce the sequel with "details to follow" and manga creator comments.

wikis.title: Blue Lock (manga, anime and adaptations)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Blue Lock: the Kodansha soccer manga, its three anime seasons, the Episode Nagi film, the August 7, 2026 live-action film, stage plays, games and reception.
wikis.body:
- Manga by Muneyuki Kaneshiro, art Yusuke Nomura; Weekly Shonen Magazine since August 1, 2018; 40 volumes as of August 2026; over 65 million copies in circulation by August 2026; won the 45th Kodansha Manga Award (shonen) in 2021. Spin-off Blue Lock: Episode Nagi (art Kota Sannomiya), June 9, 2022 to July 9, 2025, 8 volumes.
- Premise: after Japan finished 16th at the 2018 World Cup, Jinpachi Ego runs Blue Lock to create the world's greatest egotistical striker; Yoichi Isagi competes against 299 other players.
- Anime: Eight Bit; season 1 aired October 9, 2022 to March 2023 (24 episodes); Episode Nagi film released April 19, 2024 (91 minutes; theme "Stormy" by Nissy and Sky-Hi); season 2 vs. U-20 Japan aired October 5 to December 28, 2024 on TV Asahi's IMAnimation block. Season 3 titled Neo Egoist League was announced in September 2025 at "Blue Lock Egoist Fest 2025". Crunchyroll streams and dubbed the series; Toonami English dub began February 8, 2026.
- Live-action film: announced September 2025; premiered in Japan on August 7, 2026 (128 minutes); Credeus with CK Works, distributed by Toho; directed by Yusuke Taki; theme "Monstruo" by Ado.
- Stage plays: main-series stage plays from May 2023 to May 2025, Episode Nagi play November 20-30, 2025, "Re: Episode Nagi" June 11-21, 2026, and a fifth main-series play covering Neo Egoist League "scheduled to run in Q4 2026".
- Games: Blue Lock: Blaze Battle (March 1, 2024; service ending March 31, 2026); Blue Lock Project: World Champion (English April 23, 2024). Collaborations with FC Tokyo, Liverpool FC and Concacaf.
- Reception: manga best-selling in the first half of 2023 with over 8 million copies; anime praised for action, criticized for CG use; season 2 criticized for a drop in animation quality.

wikis.body:

wikis.title: Aoashi soccer anime gets a 2nd season by TMS Entertainment in 2026
wikis.summary: Anime News Network report of 2025-04-29 that the Aoashi TV anime will get a second season in 2026, animated by TMS Entertainment instead of Production I.G.
wikis.body:
- Posted 2025-04-29 by Rafael Antonio Pineda and Alex Mateo on Anime News Network (modified after posting).
- The official website for the Aoashi TV anime, based on Yugo Kobayashi's manga, revealed on Tuesday with a visual that the anime will get a second season "in 2026". TMS Entertainment will animate it instead of Production I.G, which animated season 1 in 2022.
- Story: third-year middle schooler Ashito Aoi of Ehime prefecture hides his soccer talent; Tatsuya Fukuya (as spelled in the article), veteran of the J-Club team Tokyo City Esperion and coach of its youth team, sees his talent and invites him to try out for the youth team in Tokyo.
- Season 1 premiered April 2022 and Crunchyroll streamed it. Season 1 staff: Akira Sato (director, Production I.G), Masahiro Yokotani (scripts), Masaru Yokoyama (music), soccer supervision by Kenichi Takeshita, Jun Soga and Kenji Iizuka.
- Manga: launched by Kobayashi in Weekly Big Comic Spirits in January 2015; Naohiko Ueno credited for research and original story collaboration up to volume 17. The franchise account announced on April 11 that the manga will end with chapter 410; the 40th volume will be the last, and the 39th shipped that Wednesday.
- The manga won Best General Manga at the 65th Shogakukan Manga Awards and has over 15 million copies in circulation.

wikis.summary: Anime News Network report of 2023-07-16 that a second season of the Sabikui Bisco TV anime was green-lit at the Dengeki Bunko 30th anniversary event.
wikis.body:
- Posted 2023-07-16 by Egan Loo on Anime News Network.
- The live-streamed Dengeki Bunko 30th anniversary event announced on Sunday that production on a second season of the Rust-Eater Bisco (Sabikui Bisco) TV anime, from Shinji Cobkubo's light novels, has been green-lit. No date is given.
- Season 1 premiered on Tokyo MX, BS11, Sun TV and ABEMA on January 10, 2022; Funimation and Crunchyroll streamed it, including an English dub.
- Story: post-"Rusting Wind" Japan; Bisco Akaboshi of the despised Mushroom Guardian tribe seeks the "Rust-Eating" mushroom to save his dying teacher; he meets young doctor Miro Nekoyanagi, who is searching for a countermeasure against the rust consuming his big sister.
- Season 1 staff: Atsushi Ikariya (director, at OZ), Daisuke Mataga (assistant director), Sadayuki Murai (scripts), Ai Asari and Ikariya (character design), Takeshi Ueda and Hinako Tsubakiyama (music).
- Novels: Dengeki Bunko, illustrated by K Akagishi, world-building art by mocha, launched 2018; the ninth volume to be published August 10 (2023). It was the first light novel series to top both the overall and new-work rankings of Kono Light Novel ga Sugoi in the same year.
- Manga: Yusuke Takahashi on Square Enix's Manga UP! 2019-2020; part two launched December 15, 2022 with So Natsuki replacing Takahashi as artist.
- Disclosure: Kadokawa is majority owner of Anime News Network.

wikis.title: Original Naruto anime gets four brand-new episodes for 20th anniversary
wikis.summary: Anime News Network reports that the Naruto TV anime will air four brand-new episodes starting in September, with earlier episodes rerunning in Japan from July.
wikis.body:
- Posted 2023-03-09 by Rafael Antonio Pineda (Anime News Network), sourced to the Naruto anime's official website.
- The official website announced on Thursday that the Naruto television anime will air four "brand-new" episodes starting in September to celebrate its 20th anniversary. The anime debuted in October 2002.
- Selected earlier episodes will rerun in Japan beginning in July.
- Studio Pierrot began streaming a "Road of Naruto" video in October, condensing 20 years of anime history into 10 minutes with brand new animation footage. The Boruto anime's Twitter account revealed three new visuals in October for the anniversary.
- Background: the Naruto TV anime aired from 2002 to 2007; Naruto Shippuden premiered in 2007 and ended in 2017.
- Boruto: Naruto Next Generations manga (Ukyo Kodachi, Mikio Ikemoto) launched in Weekly Shonen Jump in May 2016, moved to V Jump in July 2019; Masashi Kishimoto took over as writer in November 2020. The Boruto TV anime premiered in April 2017; Part I ends March 26, with a Part II green-lit.

wikis.title: Naruto manga and anime franchise (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga (1999 to 2014) and its anime, films, games and reception, including the postponed 20th-anniversary anime episodes.
wikis.body:
- Manga by Masashi Kishimoto in Weekly Shonen Jump, September 21, 1999 to November 10, 2014; 700 chapters, 72 volumes; 250 million copies in circulation.
- Anime: Naruto (October 3, 2002 to February 8, 2007, 220 episodes) and Naruto: Shippuden (February 15, 2007 to March 23, 2017), by Pierrot and Aniplex.
- Four "brand-new" episodes for the anime's 20th anniversary were originally scheduled for September 3, 2023 but, per the article, were postponed to a later date in August 2023.
- Franchise also includes 11 films, 12 OVAs, novels, video games and a planned live-action film; continues in Boruto.

wikis.title: Naruto: manga, plot, production, anime, films, games and reception
wikis.summary: Main body of the Wikipedia article on Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto: plot, development, media adaptations, sales and critical response.
wikis.body:
- Naruto is a Japanese manga by Masashi Kishimoto about Naruto Uzumaki, a socially isolated ninja who dreams of becoming Hokage; Part I is volumes 1 to 27, Part II volumes 28 to 72. Based on Kishimoto's one-shots Karakuri (1995) and Naruto (1997).
- Serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from September 21, 1999 to November 10, 2014; 700 chapters in 72 tankobon volumes (March 3, 2000 to February 4, 2015). Chapters 1 to 238 are Part I, 239 to 244 a Kakashi gaiden, 245 to 700 Part II (after a 2 and a half year gap). Viz Media licensed it for North America.
- Development: an early concept had Naruto as a chef; Godzilla inspired the tailed-beast mythology.
- Anime: first series directed by Hayato Date, produced by Pierrot and Aniplex, TV Tokyo, October 3, 2002 to February 8, 2007, 220 episodes (first 135 adapt Part I, remaining 85 original). Naruto: Shippuden ran February 15, 2007 to March 23, 2017. "A series of four 'brand-new' episodes, to commemorate the original anime's 20th anniversary, were originally scheduled to premiere on September 3, 2023; however, in August of that same year, it was announced that the episodes would be postponed to a later date."
- Also 11 theatrical films and 12 OVAs; a live-action film announced by Lionsgate in July 2015, with Tasha Huo announced as scriptwriter on November 27, 2023. Video games mostly fighting games; the first, Naruto: Konoha Ninpocho, released March 27, 2003 for WonderSwan Color.
- Sales: 250 million copies in circulation across 46 countries and regions; volume 28 was the top-selling manga volume of 2008 in North America; volume 7 won a Quill Award in 2006.
- Critics praised characters, storylines and action, though some felt the fights slowed the story.

- Light novel series by Shogo Kinugasa, illustrated by Shunsaku Tomose, published by Media Factory under MF Bunko J. Year 1: May 2015 to September 2019 (eleven volumes plus three short story volumes, May 25, 2015 to September 25, 2019); Year 2 (2-nensei-hen): January 2020 to November 2024; Year 3 (3-nensei-hen): began March 2025. Seven Seas Entertainment licensed it in English and on February 17, 2021 announced a new version of volume seven after localization omitted several paragraphs.
- Premise: at the government-established Tokyo Metropolitan Advanced Nurturing School, students in Classes A to D compete over three years; graduating Class A members are said to be promised their chosen career path or further education. Protagonist Kiyotaka Ayanokoji is in Class D with Suzune Horikita and Kikyo Kushida.
- Manga: Yuyu Ichino's adaptation began in Monthly Comic Alive on January 27, 2016, twelve tankobon volumes as of February 22, 2022 (Seven Seas volume 1 in February 2022); Shia Sasane's manga of the sequel novels began in December 2021.
- Anime overview: Lerche produced seasons in July to September 2017, July to September 2022, January to March 2024 and April to June 2026; "a fifth season has been announced".

wikis.title: Kaguya-sama: Love Is War (Wikipedia)
wikis.summary: Wikipedia article on Aka Akasaka's manga Kaguya-sama: Love Is War and its anime, live-action, novel and spin-off adaptations, including the announced finale film.
wikis.body:
- Japanese manga by Aka Akasaka, published by Shueisha (English: Viz Media). Serialized in Miracle Jump (May 19, 2015 to January 19, 2016), then Weekly Young Jump (March 24, 2016 to November 2, 2022); 281 chapters in 28 volumes (first March 18, 2016, last December 19, 2022).
- Premise: student council president Miyuki Shirogane and vice president Kaguya Shinomiya at Shuchiin Academy are too proud to confess, believing whoever does so first "loses"; halfway through the series they confess and the focus shifts to advancing the relationship.
- Anime: 12-episode TV series by A-1 Pictures (2019); 12-episode second season Love Is War? (2020); OVA (2021); 13-episode third season Ultra Romantic (2022); film The First Kiss That Never Ends (December 2022); TV special The Stairway to Adulthood (2025). An anime film serving as the story's conclusion, "The Final Chapter", with an original story by Aka Akasaka, "was announced" (no date given).
- Live action: film premiered September 6, 2019 (Sho Hirano, Kanna Hashimoto; director Hayato Kawai); sequel Kaguya-sama Final announced January 6, 2021, premiered August 20, 2021.
- Spin-offs: Dojin-ban manga by Shinta Sakayama (June 14, 2018 to June 25, 2020, 4 volumes); yonkoma Kaguya-sama o Kataritai by G3 Ida (July 26, 2018 to November 2, 2022, 8 volumes); two novels by Juichiro Hitsujiyama (September 19, 2018; November 17, 2023).
- Sales and awards: over 22 million copies in circulation by December 2022; 65th Shogakukan Manga Award (general category, 2020); third Next Manga Award (2017); ranked 50th in TV Asahi's Manga Sosenkyo 2021.
- Viz announced the license at San Diego Comic-Con on July 20, 2017. Akasaka's Oshi no Ko began in the same magazine April 23, 2020.
- Akasaka's stated inspirations: character names from The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter; School Rumble and Death Note-style mind battles cited.
